text:
customer-jane: Hey team — seeing streaming responses cut off mid-sentence for a customer. Client gets data for ~18s then the SSE stream just stops, no final "done" event. Reconnects automatically and resumes but the final tokens never come through. Happened 3x in last hour. Request ID: rz-9f3a. Attached pcap: s3://redwood-support/pcap/1967890123-client.pcap

support-bot: Thanks for reporting — I've created ticket SUP-1967890123 and attached the trace id. Can you confirm client, SDK, and region?

customer-jane: Using our Node SDK v1.3.2 on Ubuntu 22.04, region eu-west-1. Client is an Electron app. Happens across multiple users but same app version. No heavy local CPU.

maria-support: Thanks. A couple quick asks while we triage: 1) can you share the full request headers and the X-Request-ID? 2) can you reproduce with curl and send a tcpdump/pcap capturing the reconnect window? 3) are you using our SSE heartbeat?

customer-jane: Header snippet below. We get X-Request-ID back from Redwood as rz-9f3a. We are not adding any heartbeat events, relying on default connection behavior.

customer-jane: ```
GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
Accept: text/event-stream
User-Agent: MyClient/1.2.3
X-Client-App: electron-gen
```

tony-eng: Eva/tony from eng taking on kernel-level triage. If you can repro, please run two captures: client-side tcpdump and one from the edge proxy (if possible). On the client run:
```
sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443
```Also run curl repro to get a deterministic trace:
```
curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \   --no-buffer "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-mini&prompt=hello"
```
Include the response headers from the failing attempt.

customer-jane: Captured pcap (link above) and here's curl output from a failing run:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (12.34.56.78) port 443
> GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-mini&prompt=hello HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX
> 
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< x-request-id: rz-9f3a
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< 
:data: {"id":"msg-1","choices":[{"delta":{"text":"Hello"}}]}

:data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"text":" world"}}]}

* marked stream as done
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```Note how curl logs a "marked stream as done" even though final punctuation missing.

eva-sre: I inspected the pcap. There's a TLS-level FIN from the upstream edge at ~18.2s after response start, followed by a TLS close_notify. No RST. Client immediately reopens and issues a new GET with `if-none-match` missing (no resume tokens in our SSE flow). The server did not send a final SSE `event: done` before the FIN. I see keepalive (TCP keepalive probes) not in the window; looks like proxy idle timeout.

maria-support: Can you paste the edge logs around rz-9f3a? We need to confirm whether the proxy initiated the close due to idle, an upstream error, or a quota.

eva-sre: Edge log snippet (sanitized):```
[2026-03-14T11:23:12.912Z] rz-9f3a method=GET path=/v1/stream status=200 bytes_sent=10240 duration_ms=18234 upstream=ok proxy_event=idle_timeout limit=55s
```So proxy idle_timeout=55s triggered close at 18.2s? Wait weird metric naming. Rechecking timestamps: duration_ms=18234 => 18.234s. Looks like our internal keepalive threshold is lower than the proxy idle timer due to chunking behavior.

tony-eng: Good catch. Two hypotheses: 1) client isn't emitting SSE comment heartbeats so the proxy considers the connection idle between small chunks and triggers a close after its internal short threshold; 2) the server runtime micro-batches tokens and sometimes has >15s between actual chunks for this prompt shape, which combined with the proxy timer causes premature close. Both plausible.

maria-support: Next steps: 1) Recommend enabling client-side SSE heartbeat comments, e.g., send `: ping\n\n` every 20s from server or have client instruct server to use heartbeat (we have a heartbeat option in the SDK). 2) Temporarily extend edge idle timeout for that tenant while we investigate batching. 3) We will add clearer logging to distinguish proxy-initiated close vs server close in the response stream.

customer-jane: What's the SDK heartbeat option? We didn't know. Also can you confirm this is not a billing/quota thing?

maria-support: It's not billing — logs show status=200 and bytes_sent>0. Heartbeat in SDK: set `streamOptions.heartbeatIntervalMs = 15000` (Node SDK) which will add SSE comments like `:heartbeat\n\n` between token chunks. That keeps proxies from considering the stream idle.

tony-eng: For immediate repro, try running this Node snippet to simulate server heartbeats client-side (if you can't update server yet):```js
// quick client stub to keep connection alive
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async () => {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-mini', {
    headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-XXXX', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' },
  });
  res.body.on('data', chunk => {
    process.stdout.write(chunk);
  });
})();
```This won't add heartbeats from server but will show exact timing between chunks.

eva-sre: We also recommend capturing the TLS session close ciphers and sequence numbers to ensure no middlebox is injecting resets. In the pcap I see a clean FIN, not a reset, so it's controlled close.

customer-jane: We can flip heartbeat on. Will patch SDK to `heartbeatIntervalMs=15000` and report back. Any config we should change on our end?

maria-support: No tenant-side config needed for now. We'll also temporarily bump the edge proxy idle threshold for your org to 90s while we evaluate batching behavior. I'll coordinat with infra.

support-bot: infra-change-request IR-98234 created to bump idle_timeout for tenant "electron-gen" to 90s for 24h window.

customer-jane: Patch landed in our app (heartbeat enabled). After 2 hours of testing, no more mid-stream silent drops. Thanks — looks like heartbeat fixed the symptom.

tony-eng: We'll still follow up: 1) add a server-side SSE heartbeat option so SDKs can opt in server-side, 2) instrument runtime to emit `last_chunk_time_ms` in trace payload so we can spot long inter-chunk gaps in future.

maria-support: Closing loop: root cause = edge idle timer closing connections during rare long inter-chunk pauses combined with no heartbeat. Mitigation = enable client/server heartbeats or bump proxy timeout. Action items:
- tony-eng: add trace field for inter-chunk gap (RFC in PR  #421).
- infra: short-term bump idle_timeout for org (IR-98234).
- sdk: expose heartbeat option in all language clients and docs.

customer-jane: Appreciated. Please keep me posted when server-side heartbeat option is available so we can remove our workaround. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Will do. Marking the thread resolved for now. If you see any reoccurrence please reopen with new pcap and the x-request-id. :eyes:
